To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the transfer of an agent into a liquid food is a function of: the quality of the polymer/liquid food contact, the coefficient of convections in the liquid food, the concentration of agent in each layer and the thickness of the layers in a multilayer system.
the quality of the polymer-food contact is the most important factor to control in active packaging, and that the thickness of the polymer layers is not so important in the process of agent transfer.

the concentration of the chemical agent in the package is not uniform and depends on the thickness of the layer and the coefficient of conduction, while the concentration in the liquid food depends on the thicknesses of the different layers, the coefficient of confection and on the initial concentration of the chemical in the package.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the transfer of active substances in polymer packages for food preservation.
the study of the transfer of active agents through polymer packages, with a special focus on the kinetics of the transfer.
the study of the kinetics of the transfer of chemical or antimicrobial agent from an active polymer package to the liquid food enclosed, with the aim of prolonging the shelf life of packaged foods.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the transfer rate of the active agent is controlled by the thickness of the package, the concentration of active agent in the package, the diffusion coefficient of the agent in the package and by convections into the liquid food, with the coefficient of convective being the most important.

the quality of the polymer/liquid contact and the thickness of the polymer layer are important parameters in the design of active food packages, while the convection coefficient and the concentration of the active agent are less important.

, in order to improve the efficiency of active packages, the following parameters must be taken into consideration:- the coefficient of convections, which must be maximized, and- the thickness of each polymer layer, which must be minimized.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the quality of contact between the polymer layers and the food is a key parameter for the efficiency of the active package, and the coefficient of convections plays a significant role in the kinetics of the transfer of the agent into the liquid food.

it is important to have an accurate knowledge of the diffusion coefficient of the active agent in each polymer layer of the package, and to have a reliable estimation of the coefficient of convections in each case.
it provides a better understanding of the transfer of chemical or antimicrobial agent into food, which will help to improve the development of active packaging.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, for the same total amount of agent, the best way to deliver it is to put it into one single layer of a multi-layer system, and that the best way to control the kinetics of transfer is to increase the thickness of the layer containing the agent.
the agent concentration in each layer is not uniform, but decreases as the layer gets closer to the food.

the thickness of each of the layers of the package is a crucial parameter, and that the quality of contact between the polymer layer and the liquid food is a very important parameter, especially for the first layer of the package.
